correctness.rationale: For each adjacent fibre pair the exact mean-square identity bounds squared mean difference plus both conditional variances by 1; for each nonadjacent pair Popoviciu range-variance on the equally weighted mixture bounds squared mean difference plus twice each variance by squared index gap. Summing and using the exact pairwise variance identity yields the displayed nonnegative deficit, with endpoint and interior coefficients n-3 and n-4. All equality cases follow: n>=5 forces each conditional variance zero, and terminal saturation forces unit-slope means; n=4 endpoints are forced constant and metric interval intersections force interior constancy; n=3 has a separate exact sum of three nonnegative terms, giving balanced endpoint sign potentials. The unit-slope examples attain equality. The two-layer explicit K2,2 analysis shows the sharp transition. Exact rational finite tests directly reproduce deficits and small-class equality but do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem answers whether a path-level metric refined to arbitrarily large internal fibres preserves its natural Lipschitz-to-L2 variance norm: exact value remains unchanged for n>=3, despite new internal variation degrees of freedom and arbitrary positive conditional masses. The separate n=3 and n>=4 optimizer classifications identify a sharp structural rigidity boundary. The quantified sum-of-squares deficit supplies natural stability and shows why the conclusion is not a routine substitution of the ordinary path theorem; a two-layer counterexample proves the preservation threshold is sharp.
